findings.title: Timezone test assumes a different server default
findings.why_it_matters: The test fails on a valid PostgreSQL installation whose default TimeZone is already Africa/Nairobi, before it reaches the pooled connection assertion. This makes the pooling test suite depend on host database configuration.
evidence: The preceding SQL only reads SHOW TIMEZONE; it does not establish a known starting timezone, while `new_time_zone` is hard-coded to Africa/Nairobi.
findings.suggested_fix: Set a known contrasting session timezone before the first assertion (for example, `SET TIME ZONE 'UTC'`) or choose the target timezone based on the value read, so the pooled test doesn't depend on the PostgreSQL server's default.

testing_gaps: No test changes TIME_ZONE or USE_TZ after a pooled connection has been opened and verifies the pool is closed and recreated with the new timezone. The existing timezone test enables pooling only after closing the initial unpooled connection, so it doesn't exercise the new close_pool() path in DatabaseWrapper.ensure_timezone().
